hypothesis: If Darwin is right that the temperature of the whole world was simultaneously cooler during the Glacial period, then within one and the same dated interval of the last glaciation (the Last Glacial Maximum chronozone, 19-23 ka) surface temperature should have been below modern values everywhere: in both hemispheres, at all latitudes, and in every ocean basin, not only in the northern regions where glacial geology was first described.
pass_criterion: In the MARGO gridded compilation of LGM (19-23 ka) sea-surface temperature anomalies (modern minus LGM, annual mean, 5x5 degree cells), (i) >= 90 % of cells with data show cooling (anomaly > 0), (ii) in every 30-degree latitude band of each hemisphere with >= 5 cells, and in each of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific basins, >= 80 % of cells show cooling and the area-weighted mean anomaly is > 0 with a one-sample t-test p < 0.01, and (iii) the area-weighted global mean anomaly is >= 1 degree C.
fail_criterion: Refutes if any hemisphere, or any 30-degree band of a hemisphere with >= 5 cells, or any basin, has a majority of cells warmer than modern, or if the global fraction of cooling cells is < 60 %. Any other outcome is mixed.
interpretation: Darwin's 'Glacial period' is read as the last glaciation and 'this period' as its culmination; the MARGO project's LGM chronozone (19-23 ka, defined on independent radiocarbon and stratigraphic age models) is the standard operationalisation of a single simultaneous interval, so testing whether cooling is found in every region within that window tests simultaneity directly. 'Temperature of the whole world' is tested with sea-surface temperature because the ocean compilation is global, gridded and has quantified errors; land temperatures are not tested here. Darwin's own hedge ('or at least along broad longitudinal belts') is covered by the per-band and per-basin criteria. A cell counts as 'cooler' if the central anomaly estimate is positive; a sensitivity count using only cells whose anomaly exceeds its total error is reported but is not part of the rule.
